title: Three-Way Triangulation Analysis: Case A vs Case B vs Case C

Case_B.name: 650-Element Receiver Initialized by Nonmatching State Transfer (Pkg 51)

root_cause_diagnosis.geometric_discrepancy: The donor mesh (Case A) was pre-cracked with initial sharp slit a0 = 0.040 mm (duplicate nodes spanning x in [0.000, 0.040] mm). The 650-quad receiver mesh generator (audit_and_generate_package51.py) inadvertently defaulted to slit_a = 0.020 mm, duplicating nodes only up to x = 0.020 mm.
root_cause_diagnosis.consequence_for_case_b: In Case B (Package 51), the domain x in [0.020, 0.040] mm along y = 0.050 mm was topologically welded. Projecting the donor's open crack displacement field onto this welded ligament imposed severe artificial kinematic opening strain. During Step 1 zero-increment re-equilibration, Newton-Raphson resolved the unphysical stress by driving phase-field damage to d -> 1.0 (delta_d up to +0.9561) along the welded ligament, causing an artificial +34.88% fracture energy surge and -40.8% reaction force drop.
root_cause_diagnosis.irreversibility_reinterpretation: The 3,046 sample points with apparent damage deficit > 10^-4 in PACKAGE51_TRANSFER_AUDIT.json were clustered around the mismatched slit region (x in [0.020, 0.040] mm). This is a concrete geometric artifact of the mismatched mesh generator, NOT an intrinsic failure of nonmatching state transfer or a physical irreversibility impossibility.
root_cause_diagnosis.case_c_independent_validation: Case C (Package 52) provides the clean, uninterrupted 650-element benchmark with the bitwise-frozen production UEL (f42_mixed_uel.for). Because slit_a = 0.020 mm leaves a longer uncracked ligament (0.080 mm vs 0.060 mm), the specimen carries a much higher pre-snap reaction force (64.78 N at u = 0.00258 mm) and maintains clean monotonicity across all 50 increments with 0 cutbacks and Exit 0.
